notes: Each eval runs on a fixture repo built by evals/fixtures/build.sh. with_skill gets both skills plus the skill state the fixture defines (AGENTS.md blocks, .ai/); without_skill gets the same repo without them. Programmatic checks live in evals/grade.mjs; checks marked (judgment) are graded by reading the final message and diff. Fixtures with a state-in-baseline file (on/off evals) give without_skill the same AGENTS.md and .ai/ state, so only the skill differs. Evals 8-10 check that triggers work in Italian, French and German. Eval 11 checks per-branch handoffs with a colleague's open handoff in the repo. Eval 12 checks that a merge of develop into the feature branch after the handoff is noticed. Evals 4 and 10 keep the 0.2 single handoff and merge-from-develop keeps the 0.3 block on purpose, to cover the upgrades. Examples in the skill text deliberately differ from the eval scenarios, to avoid teaching to the test. Fixtures reuse other fixtures' base/ and history.txt through symlinks, so there is no copied source to keep in sync. Eval 13 checks that setup finds an existing ADR folder and roadmap instead of creating new places (a split goes to docs/backlog/). Eval 14 checks the end of a branch's task with docs/tasks/: the task file is deleted, the open question becomes an unassigned task, the decision is kept. Its fixture has state-in-baseline, so the baseline reads the same 0.4 block and does the same: it measures the block, and stays as a regression test. Eval 15 checks the prototype → stabilize transition: the plan is kept as prioritized open items in .ai/debt.md, and no work starts without agreement. Eval 16 runs with `project-phase: ask` in the user's global instructions (the global_instructions field, see run-prompt.md): with no answer the agent must ask in the final message and record nothing. Eval 17 checks that a confirmation in the phase.md history stops the agent from asking again for the same signal. Eval 18 checks /backlog with docs/tasks/ (an existing folder kept in the block): the branch's handoff comes first, other tasks are listed with assignee and in-progress mark, nothing is written. Eval 19 checks /backlog with GitLab issues when glab cannot reach the host (gitlab.example.com): report it with the login command, invent nothing. Eval 20 checks that setup detects a GitLab origin and proposes its issues. Fixtures with a `remote` file get it as origin (never fetched). Runs need the backlog skill in the installed skills list (run-prompt.md). Evals 21 and 22 check /backlog new (folder: one file, no assignee, done condition not invented) and /backlog close with GitLab (login first, exact close command, confirmation, nothing claimed). Evals 23 and 24 check /backlog comment: a dated line under ## Notes in a task file, and the exact glab issue note command with confirmation for GitLab. Evals 25 and 26 check Jira: setup proposes Jira project ITEMS when branch names and commit subjects repeat its key, even with origin on GitHub; /backlog close with Jira when acli cannot reach the site gives the login command and the exact acli transition command, with confirmation. Eval 27 checks /backlog filter with Jira (parent added to the JQL), eval 28 /backlog help (commands and task place, nothing listed or written), eval 29 the fixed filter of the Tasks line (new work items get --parent). Eval 30 checks /work-journal setup on a project already set up: only the Tasks line moves to Jira, the rest stays. Evals 31-33 use jira-team, whose .ai/team.md is ignored by git (extra/ with .gitignore): an alias resolves to the Jira account ID, a new work item never gets a sprint, and /backlog lists the current sprint first. Evals 34-37 check /start and /finish (fixtures start-ready and finish-ready, no git flow, develop ahead of main). Their prompt replaces "Don't commit, push or create branches" with "Don't push. Creating branches, commits and local merges is part of the task when the skills call for it." Evals 38 and 39 are the git flow variants of 34 and 36: fixtures gitflow-start and gitflow-finish set git flow's config through a git-config file (build.sh); eval 38 starts on main with develop ahead, so only git flow branches from develop; eval 39 relies on the final message, because git flow 0.4.1 leaves no trace (no hooks, no per-branch config) and the sandbox blocks writes to .git/config. Eval 40 checks the team.md auto-fill at setup; build.sh history lines take an optional fourth field, the commit author.
